verdict: Avoid new diamond and jewellery trading exposure in Mumbai for now; lend only to proven, low-leverage, bank-funded jewellers with tight stock-and-receivable controls, and decline speculative or heavily leveraged traders.
title: Mumbai diamond & jewellery trading: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What this business physically is
**A Mumbai diamond or jewellery trader buys rough or polished stones and metal, holds them as inventory, and converts them to cash through cutting, setting and sale to retailers or exporters.** Cash sits in stock and in receivables from buyers; value sits in the spread between buy and sell plus making charges. Pricing power is thin for plain trading and better for branded or design-led jewellery. The working-capital cycle is the whole business: stock turns slowly, receivables run long, and a single price move in gold or diamonds can wipe out the margin. **So when a proposal lands, check the stock-turn and receivable days first; if stock is ageing or receivables are stretching, ask why before you look at the P&L.**

## What has changed now
**The data pack calls this an AVOID at a score of 32, and the local signal is weak: Maharashtra electricity demand grew 6.0% Apr-to-date against India's 9.5%, 3.5 pp slower [D].** Against that, Maharashtra GST collections grew 8.6% Apr-to-date versus India's 6.1%, 2.5 pp faster [D] — so the state is collecting more tax even as power demand lags, which points to formalisation rather than broad demand. Nationally, bank credit is up 29.1% YoY against activity of 6.1%, a gap of 23.0 pp [D], and the repo is 5.5%, raised from 5.25% with a tightening stance [D]. **That combination means money is chasing this trade faster than it is growing, so leverage is the risk, not the opportunity.**

## Where the growth is
**The local news is about infrastructure, not demand: construction has begun on India Jewellery Park Mumbai in Navi Mumbai, Phase 1 at 24.97 lakh sq. ft. with investment potential of ₹50,000 crore [1].** Separately, HRD Antwerp has opened an office in Mumbai, and gems and jewellery trade between India and Belgium reached approximately 3.5 billion dollars in 2025-26 [2]. Peer results show where the money is being made: Vaibhav Global reported gross margin up about 197 basis points to 65.5%, with lab-grown diamonds at 12% of retail revenue and retail volumes up about 2% on lower price-point items [5]; IGIL reported consolidated PAT of ₹185.8 crore, up 43% YoY [7]. **So pursue jewellers selling lower-ticket, design-led and lab-grown pieces, and the certification and grading service providers around them; avoid plain high-value stone traders whose margin depends on a price call.**

## How to grow safely
**Structure every line as a stock-and-receivable-backed working-capital facility, not a term loan, and take the stock statement and receivable ageing every month.** Ask for the gold-metal-gold or consignment arrangement in writing; if the borrower cannot show where the stock physically sits, ask for the vault or bourse records. Take monthly GST returns and bank statements, and require a personal guarantee. **If average limit utilisation is running near the sanctioned limit, ask for the drawing-power calculation; a firm with nil utilisation of a ₹100 crore limit for twelve months to June 30, 2026 and a current ratio of 4.34x [11] is the profile you want, not the one drawing 100%.**

## Early-warning signs
**Watch stock ageing, receivable days and limit utilisation together — any two moving the wrong way at once is your exit signal.** A trader whose top customers concentrate revenue is fragile: one rated bullion business had its top five customers at 33% and 99% of gold and silver segment revenues respectively in FY2025 [8]. Note that the rating reports here are undated or old (2024 and 2025) [8][9][10], so treat them as background, not current fact. **If a borrower's sales are flat while its bank limits are fully drawn, decline the enhancement and ask for a stock audit.**
watch: GST turnover falling while borrowings rise -> reduce limit and seek receivables detail
Top-five customer share above 50% -> require diversification plan or additional collateral
Quarterly gold and diamond price movement
Sharp price fall with unsold stock -> revalue stock and top up margin
